post.hook: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO
post.subhook: Plus Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Qwen 4 Max and new pressure on AI chips

stories.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO
stories.detail: Colette Kress takes over as interim CEO of the largest AI chip supplier after an abrupt leadership change.

stories.headline: Gemini 4 Hydrogen becomes the default in Google Search
stories.detail: Now default in Search and the Gemini app; benchmarks reportedly put it near Claude Sonnet 5.5 at lower cost.

stories.headline: Congress asks Huang to testify on Nvidia's China dealings
stories.detail: Lawmakers also asked Commerce Secretary Lutnick to testify amid an alleged Chinese spy link to Huang.

stories.headline: Alibaba launches flagship Qwen 4 Max
stories.detail: Alibaba's new flagship model adds to frontier competition from China.

stories.headline: Claude can now join Google Meet calls in beta
stories.detail: Claude Meetings lets Claude sit in on video calls and draft documents during the meeting.

stories.headline: Meta's Muse agent can now call businesses for you
stories.detail: Outbound calling is available to paid subscribers in the US.

stories.headline: AlphaGenome 2 reads variants at single cell-type resolution
stories.detail: Researchers get a noncommercial API for cell-type-level genetic variant analysis.

stories.headline: US reportedly near curbs on China's remote AI chip access
stories.detail: The reported rules would limit Chinese firms' use of advanced AI compute through remote cloud access.

stories.headline: Australia proposes mandatory audits for frontier AI makers
stories.detail: If passed, frontier labs would face independent model audits and steep penalties.

post.caption:
Nvidia has a new interim CEO, and it's a heavy day for AI chips and models.

1. Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; Colette Kress is named interim CEO. (Nvidia)
2. Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen as the default in Search and the Gemini app, reportedly near Claude Sonnet 5.5 at lower cost. (Google DeepMind)
3. Congress asks Huang and Commerce Secretary Lutnick to testify on Nvidia's China dealings, amid an alleged Chinese spy link. (TechCrunch)
4. Alibaba launches its flagship Qwen 4 Max. (MobiDevices)
5. Claude Meetings brings Claude into Google Meet in beta to join calls and draft documents. (The Decoder)
6. Meta's Muse agent can now place calls to US businesses for paid subscribers. (TechCrunch)
7. AlphaGenome 2 analyzes genetic variants at single cell-type resolution, with a noncommercial API. (The Decoder)
8. The US is reportedly finalizing curbs on China's remote access to AI chips. (24/7 Wall St.)
9. Australia proposes a safety law with mandatory independent audits for frontier AI makers. (The Decoder)

Chips, policy and models all moved today. 📌

clusters.headline: Meta launches outbound calling for Muse, its AI agent, for paid US subscribers
